rules._comment: Non-veg gravy Monday and Wednesday, chicken biryani Friday - Friday is this counter's biryani day (client confirmed, and both sample weeks serve a veg biryani there too). Tuesday and Thursday are blank via tekion_nonveg_mwf. Mon/Wed exclude is_egg_dish because two egg dishes are mis-flagged is_south_chicken_gravy in the ontology.
rules.name: tekion_nonveg_by_weekday

rules._comment: 'Chinese Rice & Chinese gravy to be served on Tuesday.' Both sample weeks honour it (Chilli Garlic Fried Rice, Herbed Fried Rice).
rules.name: tekion_chinese_rice_tuesday

rules._comment: The veg-gravy half of the same Tuesday rule.
rules.name: tekion_chinese_gravy_tuesday

rules._comment: 'Paneer Gravy every wednesday.' Written '(Lunch & Dinner)'; dinner is out of scope, so this is the whole rule. Both sample weeks serve paneer then.
rules.name: tekion_paneer_gravy_wednesday

rules._comment: 'Khichdi every Thursday.' There is no is_khichdi flag; every khichdi in the ontology carries is_liquid_rice, and tekion_liquid_rice_once already caps liquid rice at one a week, so pinning Thursday lands that one there. Both sample weeks serve a khichdi on Thursday.
rules.name: tekion_khichdi_thursday

rules._comment: Client: no rice-based bread — only chapati or flavoured chapati. A one-slot slot_composition component IS 'this slot must be a matching dish' (CLAUDE.md note 20), so this pins the single bread cell to the chapati/phulka family. Bangalore carries 47 of them and none is is_rice_bread, so ricebread_gap_10d can no longer bite: the dosa/idli family is simply never chosen.
rules.name: tekion_bread_chapati_only

rules._comment: Chinese Tuesday serves a north or south Indian veg dry, whichever suits the rest of that day's menu — not a gobi manchurian beside the Chinese rice and gravy. Same shape a continental day already has by default (the themed veg is the gravy, the veg dry stays Indian). Per-key merge, so the city rule's exempt_slots are inherited untouched.
rules.name: theme_cuisine_filter

rules._comment: Client's protein-source list: at least one dish a day whose key_ingredient is one of these, anywhere across flavoured rice / veg gravy / veg dry / salad / dal. Selected on key_ingredient because that is how the client specified it. daily_min (not min) so it means 'every day' whatever the horizon length; it is capped per day to what that day can place, so a thin day relaxes instead of going INFEASIBLE. Variant spellings (channa_dal, gram_dal, cottage_cheese, soppu_moong, allesande, kofta_made_from_lentil) were folded into these canonical values by scripts/protein_key_ingredients.py. Not covered because Bangalore carries no such dish: soya chaap, moong chilla; pesarattu exists but is filed as bread, not one of the five slots.
rules.name: tekion_protein_source_daily

rules._comment: The protein must not always be the dal. At least 3 days a week carry one OUTSIDE the dal slot — the three ordinary (non-chinese, non-biryani) days. HARD, and `min` is auto-capped to the days that can actually place a match, so it degrades instead of going INFEASIBLE. The chinese and biryani days are pushed for by the companion soft rule rather than mandated here: every day can supply one today, but forcing all five would trade a whole plan for one dish the moment another rule disagrees.
rules.name: tekion_protein_outside_dal

rules._comment: 'these 2 days also can possibly have without breaking rules' — the chinese and biryani days. Soft twin of the floor above: one penalty per day with no non-dal protein, so the solver takes all five whenever nothing else has to give, and yields when something does. priority medium keeps it under the theme and high-tier rules.
rules.name: tekion_protein_outside_dal_all_days
